scenes.title: 1920 Johns Hopkins Nursery Table: Tame Porcelain White Rat, Wooden Control Blocks & Suspended 4-Foot Steel Bar
scenes.era: 1920, Phipps Clinic nursery room, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore

layout.description: Sunlit 1920 Baltimore hospital nursery room with tall paned windows, a raised white-sheeted padded testing table at center, neutral wooden toy blocks, an articulated matte-white porcelain tame rat sculpture and white rabbit sculpture, and behind the table's head end a suspended 4-foot steel bar with a wooden-handled claw hammer.

positions.who: Rosalie Rayner (mannequin in 1920 white nurse-style laboratory smock)
positions.where: kneeling beside the raised white padded table gently placing the articulated matte-white porcelain rat sculpture beside wooden blocks
seated on the white padded mattress reaching curiously at baseline, then pulling hand back toward wooden blocks after the steel-bar clang

positions.who: John B. Watson (mannequin in 1920 dark wool suit behind a weißen white coat)
positions.where: standing out of the infant's sightline behind the head of the table holding the hammer beside the suspended 4-foot steel bar

props.name: suspended 4-foot steel bar & carpenter's claw hammer
props.period_detail: iron rod hung from ceiling cord behind the padded table head
props.physical_behavior: the exact acoustic unconditioned startle source from Watson & Rayner 1920

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain tame rat & white rabbit sculptures
props.period_detail: porcelain animal figures placed gently on the white cotton mattress
props.physical_behavior: neutral baseline animals turned into conditioned and generalized cues

props.name: wooden toy blocks & hand-cranked 1920 35mm cinema camera
props.period_detail: neutral control blocks Albert still played with calmly plus archival film camera
props.physical_behavior: separates cue-specific conditioning from general distress

actions.verb_sequence: reaches forward calmly toward the matte-white porcelain rat at baseline -> Watson taps the suspended steel bar behind the table -> on the next silent trial, Infant pulls hand back from the porcelain rat while still stacking wooden blocks calmly
places the white porcelain rabbit and fuzzy white mask for the 5-day generalization check while logging session notes

reactions.reaction: leans away from furry cues while remaining calm with wooden control blocks
record both generalization and the ethical omission of any final extinction session

scenes.wardrobe: 1920 Baltimore clinic attire: white cotton clinical smock over long skirt; 1920 wool suit under lab coat; infant white cotton romper.
scenes.recognition_hook: At nine months he reached calmly for every animal in the room — seven clangs of a hidden steel bar turned silent white fur into an instant retreat.

key_visual.description: a 1920 white-sheeted nursery testing table with an infant figure, a matte-white porcelain rat sculpture and wooden blocks in front, and a researcher standing behind with a suspended 4-foot steel bar and hammer

scenes.title: Stimulus Generalization vs Wooden Control Blocks (Day +5)

layout.description: Same sunlit white padded table displaying wooden blocks beside a white porcelain rabbit sculpture, cotton wool tuft, and bearded mask.

positions.where: alternating wooden blocks (happy reach) with white furry items (hesitant pull-back)

props.name: wooden control blocks vs white bearded mask & cotton wool
props.period_detail: proves withdrawal tracked furry similarity rather than general room distress

actions.verb_sequence: offers wooden blocks -> Infant stacks them calmly -> places white porcelain rabbit -> Infant leans back

reactions.reaction: notes fading strength over weeks in lab diary

scenes.recognition_hook: Right between pulling back from white fur, Albert stacked wooden blocks happily — proving the alarm tracked fur similarity, not the room.

scenes.title: 1924 Antidote: Mary Cover Jones & 'Little Peter' Exposure Cure
scenes.era: 1924, Columbia Teachers College nursery, New York

layout.description: Sunlit cheerful playroom where a child enjoys a snack tray at one end of a long room while a calm white porcelain rabbit sits safely 12 feet away.

positions.who: Mary Cover Jones (mannequin in 1924 cardigan and blouse)
positions.where: gradually moving the caged matte-white porcelain rabbit one foot closer per day only while young Peter stays relaxed with snacks and calm playmates
smiling and eventually patting the porcelain rabbit with zero fear

props.name: step-by-step distance markers (12 ft -> 6 ft -> 0 ft) & snack tray
props.period_detail: first experimental cure of childhood animal fear via graduated counterconditioning
props.physical_behavior: the humane ethical answer to Little Albert

actions.verb_sequence: inches the porcelain rabbit closer across safe daily steps -> Child calmly touches the rabbit

scenes.recognition_hook: Watson showed fear could be wired in; four years later Mary Cover Jones invented graduated exposure therapy to gently wire it OUT.

scenes.title: The Textbook Myth Audit & Modern IRB Child Safeguards

layout.description: Bright archive reading table comparing Watson & Rayner's original 1920 pages and hospital census ledger beside red-lined introductory textbooks.

positions.where: cross-checking the 1920 film log and 1919 hospital census against exaggerated textbook paragraphs

props.name: 1920 original journal vs corrected textbook myths & IRB Ethics Charter
props.period_detail: exposes invented 'teddy bear' myths and enshrines informed consent & debriefing

actions.verb_sequence: highlights fading fear notes in 1920 diary and places IRB child-protection charter beside it

reactions.reaction: appreciates checking primary data over secondary folklore

scenes.recognition_hook: Over half of textbooks exaggerated what happened — and Little Albert's unreversed test helped forge modern research ethics.
